cards.front: Recall a key point about Manufacturing Processes
cards.back: Injection moulding: thermoplastic melted and forced into a steel mould under high pressure - mass production, high tooling cost, very low per-unit cost, complex 3D shapes. Used for LEGO bricks, bottle caps, phone cases.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Manufacturing Processes
cards.back: CNC machining: computer-controlled cutting from solid stock - precision, prototyping and batch production, no mould cost, but slower per unit and creates waste (swarf).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Manufacturing Processes
cards.back: Blow moulding: extruded polymer tube inflated against a mould - produces hollow shapes (bottles). Extrusion: continuous profile pushed through a die - pipes, window frames.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Manufacturing Processes
cards.back: Metal forming: press forming (sheet metal pressed between die and punch - car body panels), die casting (molten metal forced into a mould), sand casting (sand mould for one-offs/small batches).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Manufacturing Processes
cards.back: Timber processing: planing (smooth flat surfaces), routing (profiles, grooves, joints), turning (lathe - chair legs, bowls), laser cutting (precision, prototyping, minimal waste).

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For manufacturing process questions: 1) State the process, 2) Name suitable materials, 3) Describe the process steps, 4) Identify appropriate production volume, 5) Evaluate advantages and limitations.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: 3D printing will replace all other manufacturing processes because it can make anything. A company needs to produce 50,000 identical ABS remote control casings. Compare injection moulding and vacuum forming, justifying the most appropriate process with reference to cost, quality and production rate.

AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). For grade 9, demonstrate detailed knowledge of manufacturing processes and perceptive evaluation of cost-quality-volume trade-offs.
